title: Construction and demolition waste in Austria

current_state.value: 11.05 million t non-hazardous mineral construction and demolition waste generated in 2023 (about 1,200 kg per inhabitant), plus 38.1 million t excavation material; together 73% of Austria's 67.2 million t total waste. Of the 11.05 Mt about 8 Mt became recycled construction materials, 825,000 t (7.5%) were landfilled. Eurostat 2022 (env_wastrt, W121, computed from treatment data): 69.2% recycled, 21.2% backfilled, 9.7% landfilled.

target.value: Official: Waste Framework Directive Art. 11(2)(b), 70% material recovery incl. backfilling (met, 90%). Proposed by the Commons: recycling excluding backfilling from 69% to 80%, landfill below 5%, generation held below 1,000 kg per inhabitant.

boundary: none directly; indirect: climate (substitution of cement and primary aggregates), land (landfill and quarry footprint)
context: Building and digging produce three quarters of Austria's waste. Rubble is mostly recycled already, but a fifth of it only goes into backfilling and a tenth to landfill. The excavation stream is three times larger than the rubble and mostly ends up in landfills. The mass shrinks only because construction is in recession. Note: Eurostat's official recovery-rate indicator (cei_wm040) was withdrawn; the rates here are computed from env_wastrt.
